Subject: POC capacity planning: VenturoTech - initial recap

Hi Sara - thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for the POC so we can align on success criteria and capacity planning.

High-level success criteria (from today's call):
- End-to-end latency: 95th percentile under 300ms for our targeted inference (chat completions, 1-2k tokens/session).
- Throughput: sustain 120-150 req/s during business hours; handle bursts to ~300 req/s for short periods (5-15min).
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate for token generation and <1% fallback to lower-cost model.
- Observability: per-request latency and token-level cost visible in dashboard; logs for audit.

Initial capacity recommendation (to start POC):
- Reserved capacity: 4 x A100-40GB GPUs (dedicated pool) - predictable throughput for baseline traffic.
- Autoscale / burst policy: allow up to +6 GPUs for burst capacity (max total = 10 GPUs) with scale decisions based on sustained queue length / GPU utilization. Typical scale-up time 90-180s depending on warm cache; we recommend a short pre-warm run prior to business hours to seed KV cache.
- Warm standby: keep 1 warm replica allocation to reduce cold-start impact during short bursts.

Estimate: this configuration should comfortably meet the 120-150 req/s baseline and provide headroom for the 300 req/s short bursts. I'll attach a short POC_capacity_plan_v1.pdf with the sketch and cost delta for burst usage.

Open items / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm the expected sustained req/s and the expected peak burst duration (typical and max)?
2) Who from VenturoTech will own the POC on your side (engineering + ops contacts)?
3) Are there any network/VPC constraints for Private deployment we should account for?

Proposed timeline: 3-week POC starting week of 2027-04-17 (flexible), milestones: kickoff + baseline tests (week 1), throughput & burst testing + tuning (week 2), evaluation & handoff (week 3).

Next steps: once you confirm the items above we can lock the reserved capacity and share the redwood-poc-config.yaml stub for your ops team to review.

Thanks - happy to jump on a quick 30-min follow-up if useful.

Subject: Re: POC capacity planning: VenturoTech - autoscale and warmup details

Sara - hi, Ethan from Solutions Engineering here. Wanted to run through the technical details you asked about and give a concrete autoscale + warm-standby recommendation for the POC.

1) Scale-up timing and behavior:
- Baseline: reserved 4 x A100 (dedicated) are always online and ready - no cold-start for those.
- Autoscale adds GPUs as additional nodes attached to the same model serving pool. Typical VM/GPU provision + runtime attach: 60-120s for cloud cold-start; effective readiness for steady throughput (including model weights loaded) ~90-180s depending on image cache.
- Cold KV cache effect: Newly attached replicas have empty KV caches. For LLama-family/decoder models the KV cache warms as requests hit. We mitigate this by: (a) keeping 1 warm standby (a small kept-warm allocation that has model weights loaded but is not fully routed for traffic) and (b) issuing short synthetic preload requests during scale-up to seed embeddings/KV as part of the autoscale flow. That typically brings response latency in line after the first 1-2 requests.

2) Recommended POC autoscale policy (config we usually use):
- keep_warm_replicas: 1 (always loaded, minimal cost footprint)
- scale_metric: gpu_utilization + request_queue
- scale_up_threshold: 75% utilization sustained for 30s or queue > 20 requests for 15s
- scale_step: add 2 GPUs per scale event
- max_additional_gpus: 6 (max total GPUs during burst = 10)
- cooldown: 120s after scale up before scaling further; scale down when utilization < 40% for 90s

3) Cost/ops note:
- Keeping 1 warm replica increases baseline cost but reduces user-perceived cold-starts for short bursts. For your traffic profile (5-12min spikes up to 320 req/s) we recommend reserved 4 GPUs + 1 warm replica + autoscale up to +6 GPUs. In our estimate that keeps most bursts below a 2-3 request latency penalty and avoids repeated scale churn.

4) Long context impact:
- Longer contexts (2k tokens) increase memory pressure and KV footprint. That means each new replica requires proportionally longer to warm for token-heavy workloads. Our preload flow seeds the most common recent prefixes to reduce this. We can also recommend a targeted cache-seeding script that replays a small set of representative prompts during scale-up to speed warmup.

Attachment: redwood-poc-config.yaml (sample autoscale + reserved config)

POC timeline & ownership (proposed):
- Kickoff: 2027-04-17 - baseline validation (Marissa owner + VenturoTech: Sara + Sandeep)
- Week 2: burst testing (we will run synthetic load profiles matching your spreadsheet) - Ethan owns test harness setup
- Week 3: evaluation, metrics collection, and contract/placement recommendations - Vivek leads cost review
